analysisDescription: I was trying to remember how I played the game. Opened the wiki to search the correct description.

dimension.title: Complementarity
dimension.description: Complementarity, extended from Rocha et. al rocha2008game, corresponds to when player actions are designed to balance each other’s weaknesses or so that strengths complement each other. It is typically achieved through asymmetric game design, with each player bringing something to the shared experience.

dimensionExamples.example: The players can do anything thing in the same time,

dimension.title: Concurrent Collaboration
dimension.description: In concurrent collaboration, players have to perform gameplay tasks concurrently.

dimension.title: Limited
dimension.description: When Limited, the game restricts communication, while not prohibiting it as a whole. It can be achieved through gameplay mechanics such as designated time/space when communication is allowed, or through allowing communication through only specific modalities only (e.g. pings, emotes); or through rules that the players should follow (e.g. do not communicate your exact position).

dimension.title: Text Chat
dimension.description: Support for players to communicate using text

dimension.title: Emotes
dimension.description: Players can communicate through particular animations their characters have (e.g. pointing at something)

dimension.title: Grouping
dimension.description: Grouping refers to activities that require a certain number of players to be accessed/completed.

dimension.title: Piggy-Backing
dimension.description: Piggy-Backing refers to a specific mechanic, where one player's performance can be leveraged for others to bypass challenges.

dimension.title: Consumables
dimension.description: Consumables refer to items that exist in a limited amount and can be utilised by players to invoke an effect (usually existing as a form of currency, materials, or food) or are not consumed on purpose by players but support the gameplay (e.g., health, energy). Consumables are shared when the agency to consume and manage them pertains to more than one player.

dimension.title: Interactables
dimension.description: Interactables refer to virtual objects and non-player characters/entities within the environment that respond to players’ actions. Interactables can be moved, shaped, or activated (e.g., a cannon that shoots when the player interacts with it). In some cases, interactables are also consumable (e.g., food in Overcooked is transported and modified as an interactable, but also consumed to complete the recipes). Interactables are shared when their state and attributes can be affected by more than one player.

dimension.title: Space
dimension.description: Space is also a resource as it defines the various places in the environment that a player can occupy and interact with. Space is shared when its utilisation is affected or constrained by others' presence or by others’ actions.

dimensionExamples.example: The player can invite their friend to join the game as a townspeople like himself.

dimension.title: Party Creation
dimension.description: Party Creation encompasses all games where groups are defined by the players themselves prior to initiating gameplay, typically leveraging friend lists or co-located party creation.

dimensionExamples.example: The player can do all the thing which it wants.

dimension.title: No Goal Structure
dimension.description: No Goal Structure is also a possibility. In some games, the experience in itself is the goal (e.g. simulation games), while in others, the expectation is for player-driven goals to emerge.

dimension.title: Party
dimension.description: Party progression results from the contributions of a group of players that opted to play together, where part of the progress is solely associated with that group (not shared with the rest of the server or community).

dimension.title: Individual
dimension.description: Individual progression is defined by individual choice and the individual impact of the progression. In-game activities can vary from individual to fully cooperative but progression affects the individual.

dimension.title: Single
dimension.description: Single applies to any game where players have control of one single entity.

dimension.title: Distinct
dimension.description: Distinct means that each player controls a different entity or set of entities

dimension.title: Arbitrary
dimension.description: Arbitrary means that all player entities are equal in their ability to act upon the world. If a selection exists, it is merely an aesthetic choice.

dimensionExamples.example: The skill of the play can grow up.

dimension.title: Customisable
dimension.description: Customisable encompasses all games with upgrades, levelling systems, and others that give players the ability to create and modify their representation throughout the game.

dimension.title: Sidekick
dimension.description: Sidekick, a second (or third, etc) player, will take the role of a different entity with typically a subset or complementary skills anchored on the main entity of the game attributed to the first player.

dimension.title: Teammates
dimension.description: Teammates, where players within a team need to coordinate their actions, abilities, and roles in order to reach a common goal against at least another team.

dimension.title: Shared
dimension.description: Shared world views apply to a game when players have access to the same world.

dimension.title: Distinct world
dimension.description: Distinct world views correspond to the players having access to entirely different worlds, and thus different perspectives and instances of them.

dimension.title: Distinct
dimension.description: Distinct refers to when each player has control of their own individual viewpoint, typically through separate screens.

dimension.title: Free Collaboration
dimension.description: In free collaboration, players can take on available tasks as they wish and decide how to contribute.

dimension.title: Abilities
dimension.description: Abilities, as described by Harris et al. 2016, are where one player can do things another player cannot. In games where these actions synergise or are complementary, it incentivises collaboration.
